content:
Hi all, I've released an AI-assisted Lean 4 formalization of a recent theorem of Antoniuk, Prorok, and Salia (arXiv:2607.00212, posted 30 June 2026): every finite admissible simple graph admits a strong majority edge-coloring with five colors.

For an edge e, "strong majority" means that, for each color, at most half of the edges adjacent to e receive that color. Admissibility excludes an edge whose endpoint degrees are 1 and 2; for finite simple graphs, this is the only obstruction to the existence of such a coloring. The conjectured optimal universal bound, due to Kalinowski, Kamyczura, Pilśniak, and Woźniak, is four.

The Lean proof is not a transcription of the paper's equitable-coloring argument. It uses a chain-contraction reduction whose core is Vizing's theorem for simple graphs with Δ ≤ 4, together with separate treatment of parallel classes and extension back along the contracted chains.

The theorem statement and the original paper were available during the work. This is therefore a verification and an alternative proof route, not an independent discovery of the theorem.

The final declaration is SMaj.Synthesis.maj_le_five. Its #print axioms output is exactly [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound], so its transitive dependency closure contains no sorryAx. The proof also does not use native_decide. The Lean environment is pinned, and the artifact includes clean rebuild instructions and notes connecting the formal statement to the paper's definitions.

  • Overview and statement-fidelity notes
  • Source and rebuild instructions
  • Final theorem declaration
  • Verification paper
  • Archival DOI

AI assistance was substantial: models contributed materially to the proof construction and Lean implementation, and the writeup gives a model-by-model account. I audited the definitions and final statement and take responsibility for the work. The artifact is kernel-checked, but the work has not yet received external review.

Feedback on the statement bridge or on the verification and provenance presentation would be particularly useful.

A technical and upstreaming note: the development contains SimpleGraph-based infrastructure for proper edge colorings, present and missing colors, Kempe graphs and swaps, Kierstead paths, and Vizing's theorem at Δ ≤ 4.

Mathlib main already has SimpleGraph.EdgeLabeling, and mathlib4#33313 is developing the proper edge-coloring API via colorings of the line graph, with Vizing listed as future work. My current development instead uses a direct Sym2-based coloring interface.

I would especially appreciate guidance on whether the Kempe/Kierstead/Vizing layers should be ported directly to the current #33313 API, or first separated as lemmas about EdgeLabeling together with a properness predicate.

For comparison, Arohee Bhoja's verified Misra–Gries development establishes the full Vizing bound using a separate computational graph representation. I could not find a prior proof-assistant formalization of Kierstead paths; pointers to one would be welcome.

Formalization-level reading of arXiv v1 also exposed one omitted restoration case and two minor/editorial issues in the written proof. None affects the theorem. I sent the authors the issue descriptions and a repair before publishing the notes.

John Erlbacher said:

I would especially appreciate guidance on whether the Kempe/Kierstead/Vizing layers should be ported directly to the current #33313 API, or first separated as lemmas about EdgeLabeling together with a properness predicate.

You haven't stated your goal so it's hard to tell, but IMO porting would be best, similar to how it makes more sense to prove that a graph is G.Colorable n and not ∃ f : V → Fin n, ∀ u v, G.Adj u v → f u ≠ f v.
Although note that #33313 is still in flux and the plan is to change EdgeColorable to take a cardinal (as you can see from the review comments).

John Erlbacher said:

Vizing listed as future work

FWIW this is still my plan after edge coloring merges.

btw, #39505

Thanks, that's exactly the guidance I needed. I'll target the #33313 API directly rather than going through EdgeLabeling first, and I'll wait for it to merge (and for the EdgeColorable-to-cardinal change to settle) before opening anything.

Good to know Vizing after the merge is your plan — in that case I won't duplicate it. My Δ ≤ 4 version exists if it's ever useful as a reference, but I'd rather contribute the pieces you're not already covering: the Kempe chain and Kierstead path machinery. I'll follow #33313 and #39505 and time my PRs around them.

Snir Broshi said:

Since you intend to contribute to Mathilb, have you read #use-of-ai?

Yes, absolutely. It's important for me to follow all rules regarding AI use, disclosure and contribution because my project is formed on the basis of modern, machine assistance and I cannot allow a hit to my credibility. You can read more here about my project.

This also won't be my first PR, you can view that here: #41523. If you see any way at all I can disclose better or improve the quality of my work, please don't hesitate to inform me and I would be happy to fix it.
